raw_response:
## Best documented match: ZunShot on Windows 11

[ZunShot](https://www.bandicam.com/zunshot/) is the strongest documented match I found for capturing one window while leaving the background outside its rounded corners transparent. Its official product page explicitly describes that behavior.

Use **Window** on the Capture tab, or **Shift+PrtScn**, then select the desired window. You can also choose it from the window list. Keep the Windows 11 rounded-corner option enabled and save as **PNG** or **WebP**. The [official capture guide](https://www.bandicam.com/zunshot/guide/capture-window/) explains that JPG loses transparency, some clipboard pastes lose it, and a window partly off-screen is captured only where visible.

This is a documentation-based recommendation, not a claim that I ran the application. I did not establish Qt6 or Fedora support for it. Your tangential section makes those preferences rather than prerequisites, so they do not disqualify an otherwise matching Windows tool.

## Alternatives, in order of relevance

### 2. Spectacle — worth checking for the KDE side

Spectacle's [official handbook](https://docs.kde.org/stable_kf6/en/spectacle/spectacle/using.html) documents Active Window and Window Under Cursor capture. This makes it a directly relevant KDE candidate. However, the evidence I could inspect did not establish the precise rounded-corner transparency result on Fedora 45 Wayland. I would keep it on the shortlist with that verification outstanding, rather than promise a complete match.

The decisive check is whether a saved window-mode PNG has transparent outside-corner pixels. A positive result supports that tested setup; retained background pixels would make that setup unsuitable.

### 3. ksnip — closest documented coverage of several preferences

The [ksnip README](https://github.com/ksnip/ksnip/blob/master/README.md) describes a Qt-based application with command-line capture and Windows, Plasma Wayland and macOS coverage. Its backend table lists Windows active-window capture and Plasma Wayland window-under-cursor capture. I could not establish Qt6 specifically or the needed corner-alpha behavior on the requested OS versions. It remains a candidate to verify, not a confirmed cross-platform answer.

### 4. ShareX — a Windows lead requiring a current-version check

The [official-project issue](https://github.com/ShareX/ShareX/issues/5667) discusses transparent Windows 11 window capture and distinguishes active-window capture from selecting a window through region mode. The old discussion also contains conflicting reports about actual transparency. That leaves the exact current settings and alpha output unresolved; it does not establish a general failure.

### 5. Greenshot — another unresolved Windows alternative

The [official-project issue](https://github.com/greenshot/greenshot/issues/326) records an attempted Windows 11 fix for version 1.3.238, followed by inconsistent results. This is insufficient evidence to recommend current Greenshot confidently for your exact corner requirement, but also insufficient to rule out every current build.

**My practical choice is ZunShot for the documented Windows behavior, with Spectacle as the first candidate to verify on your KDE system.** I found no fully verified single application satisfying all the preferred platforms and Qt6 alongside the mandatory capture behavior. The live product documentation I used is undated, so I cannot establish that every described feature was already available on November 17, 2026.
